requirements.sourceText: A. Core Courses (9 credits) - Students must take the following Core Course: GLI 211 - Perspectives in Globalization Studies and International Relations 3 credits. Students must also take two courses out of the following options: GLI 320 - Global, Cultural, and Environmental Issues 3 credits; GLI 330 - Global, Political, and Economic Issues 3 credits; GLI 340 - Conflict Resolution, Coalition Building, and Peacemaking 3 credits

notes.text: The minor is open to all undergraduates regardless of academic major or place of residence.

Students should choose a Global Interaction Area and a Specialized Global Issue Track. Students should consult with the program advisor (gli@stonybrook.edu) as soon as possible and plan their course of study. Students are encouraged to declare the minor before the start of their sophomore year but no later than the first semester of their junior year. The minor takes approximately 4 semesters (fall/spring) to complete.

Students are strongly encouraged to participate in study abroad programs. With the approval of the program advisor, credits earned for courses taken abroad may count toward fulfillment of the minor. The minor is part of the Undergraduate Academy for Globalization Studies and International Relations, and students are encouraged to participate in its enrichment opportunities.
